rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future form indicates they had not yet made this claim when these verses were revealed; it foretells a certain later utterance and a new act of unbelief.
rows.anchor: buyurulmasından anlaşılıyor ki bunlar bunu bu âyetlerin nüzûlü hengâmında daha söylememişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction was fulfilled; the parallel Nahl verse uses the past tense, which Elmalılı cites as proof that the Quran is truthful revelation from God.
rows.anchor: âyeti mâzî sîgasıyla bu tahakkuku beyan etmiştir ki bunlar Kur’ân’ın min indillah bir vahy-i sâdık olduğunda ne kadar sarihtir

rows.speaker: müşrikler
rows.claim: The polytheists argue that if Allah had willed otherwise, neither they nor their forefathers would have practiced shirk or forbidden anything.
rows.anchor: o şirki itiyad etmiş olan müşrikler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı grants the conditional point: God could have deprived them of choice, compelled faith, or prevented shirk; the proper conclusion would be to accept their punishment.
rows.anchor: Ya bize ihtiyar vermez, hepimizi imana muztar kılar veya tevfik nasip eder, imanı ihtiyar ettirir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says they turn divine willing in the past into supposed divine approval, deny that shirk and prohibition are sins, and demand that God forcibly stop them while they continue by choice.
rows.anchor: Fakat siyaktan anlaşıldığına göre onlar bunu itiraza vesile ittihaz ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created events do not entail God's approval, absence of harm, or compulsion: divine will lets fire burn, poison kill, and liars lie without making harm or falsehood good.
rows.anchor: ve meselâ Allah’ın meşiyyetiyle ateşin insanı yakabildiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot infer that future acts are approved from past events, since God's future decree is unknown; prior child-killing and rejection of prophets had manifest harms, so denying those harms is false.
rows.anchor: istikbâle ta‘alluk eden meşiyyet-i ilâhiyenin ve hükm-i kaderin insanlar için gāib ve meçhul olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reasoning contradicts itself: they invoke God's sole creative rule while deriving shirk from tawhid, prohibition from permission, and compulsion from divine will, despite having no proof for shirk or prohibition.
rows.anchor: tevhidden şirki, tahlilden tahrîmi, meşiyyetten cebri istihrac ve isbâta kalkışmanın nasıl bir tenakuz olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve promptly recognized their fault, confessed, repented, and sought God's forgiveness and mercy rather than despairing.
rows.anchor: Derhâl vaziyeti takdir ve hatalarını itiraf ve tevbe ve istiğfâra müsâra‘atle rahmet-i ilâhiyeye dehâlet eylediler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies their supplicatory words with the words Adam received from his Lord in Baqara 2:37.
rows.anchor: müsâra‘atle rahmet-i ilâhiyeye dehâlet eylediler ki bu kelimât-ı tazarru‘Sûre-i Bakara’da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing Adam and Eve's answer with Iblis's earlier reply reveals divine grace in inspiring Adam's words and a deep difference between Adam's nature and Iblis's essence.
rows.anchor: İblis’in zikri sebk eden cevâbıyla Âdem ve Havvâ’nın bu cevaplarını mukayese etmeli de bu kelimâtın derhâl kalb-i Âdem’e sünûhu ne büyük bir lutf-i ilâhî olduğunu

rows.speaker: Denilmiştir
rows.claim: A report says Adam prospered by admitting disobedience, remorse, self-blame, swift repentance, and hope in mercy; Iblis failed by denying sin, lacking remorse, blaming God, and despairing.
rows.anchor: Denilmiştir ki Âdem beş şey ile bahtiyar oldu: Muhalefeti itiraf, nedâmet, nefsini levm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a sin against a divine command or prohibition is forgiven, it still lowers its perpetrator from the rank of absolute purity.
rows.anchor: emir veya nehy-i ilâhîye muhalefetle işlenen herhangi bir günah mağfur bile olsa sâhibini nezâhet-i mutlaka mertebesinden indirmeye sebep olmaktan hâlî kalmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent assigns them an earthly dwelling and provision for a limited time, amid enmity among them.
rows.anchor: ve size arzda bir vakte kadar bir istikrar ve temettu‘var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On earth humanity will live and die, then be brought out for resurrection; God has thus established the human species on earth.
rows.anchor: ve yine ondan çıkarılacaksınız, ba‘s ü neşr olunacaksınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A satanic nuzgh is a provocation, such as anger or another agitation meant to divert a person from what God commands.
rows.anchor: yani seni emrolunduğunun hilâfına sevk etmek için kızdırmak veya diğer bir suretle tehyic etmek isteyecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When provoked, seek God's protection inwardly or aloud, recalling the greatness of His blessing and the severity of His punishment.
rows.anchor: nimetinin büyüklüğünü ve ikābının şiddetini düşünüp hıfz u inâyetine ilticâ ederek gönlünden veya dilinle gönlünle isti‘âze et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the spoken plea for refuge and knows the plea held in the heart.
rows.anchor: Muhakkak ki Allah Semî‘dir, kavlen isti‘âzeni işitir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a trace of Satan touches the God-fearing, they remember refuge in God, recognize the error and satanic trick, and guard themselves.
rows.anchor: hemen gözlerini açarlar hata noktasını ve Şeytan’ın hilesini görür, ihtiraz ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although addressed to the Messenger, the passage also gives a general address to all believers.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet, Resûlullah’a olan bu hitâbâtın bütün mü’minlere hitâb-ı âm olduğuna bir tenbîhi ihtivâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' brethren are human devils, companions and intimates of the hidden jinn devils.
rows.anchor: Şeytanların ihvânı olanlar yani gizli şeytanların kardeşleri, enîsleri olan ins şeytanları ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human devils aid the jinn in misguidance and, unlike the God-fearing, do not restrain themselves; they sink further into error and destruction.
rows.anchor: kısamaz müttakīler gibi kendilerini çekemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During a pause in revelation, opponents taunt the Prophet for not producing a sign, implying that he cobbles the Quran together himself and thereby attacking his prophethood; this is a satanic prompting.
rows.anchor: derler ki böyle demekle diğer âyetleri de Peygamber’in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger answers that he follows only revelation: the Quran is insight from the Lord and guidance and mercy for those who believe, so it deserves reverence and faith.
rows.anchor: ben hiçbir şeye değil, ancak Rabbimden bana vahyolunana ittibâ‘ederim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to listen and be silent applies when Quran is recited in prayer, a sermon, or any gathering.
rows.anchor: Kur’an kıraat edildiği vakit namazda veya hutbede veya herhangi mecliste

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silence enables attentive listening, which brings insight, faith, and action; faith and action lead to divine mercy and blessing.
rows.anchor: susmak iyi dinlemeye, iyi dinlemek basirete, basiret iman ve amele, iman ve amel de rahmet ve ni‘met-i ilâhiyeye sebep ve tarîktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qira'a is a voluntary human act: an intentional sound made by a rational speaker through specific articulation points, joined to intention and understanding.
rows.anchor: Kıraat ise bir lisan fi‘l-i ihtiyârîsidir ki âkil ve nâtık bir insanın ağzından mehâric-i mahsûsaya itimad ile çıkan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel performs iqra, making the Quran recited, rather than qira'a himself; God's act is revelation and the creation of recitation.
rows.anchor: Cibrîl’in fiili bile kıraat değil bir ikrâ, yani kıraat ettirmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An echo or reflected sound is not Quran recitation, so recitation rules such as the prostration of recitation do not follow from it; silent reading is not recitation either.
rows.anchor: fukahâ bir kıraatin aksinden hâsıl olan sadâ-yı mün‘akise kıraat ve tilâvet hükmü terettüb etmeyeceğini ve meselâ secde-i tilâvet lâzım gelmeyeceğini beyan etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gramophone or radio replay is only the reflected trace of a recitation, not a recitation itself, so the specific duty to listen and be silent does not attach to it.
rows.anchor: bir kıraat değil, bir kıraatin aksi ve tayfıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That replay need not be heard as an obligatory or recommended recitation does not make listening impermissible or make refusal obligatory; playing Quran as an instrument is improper.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı çalmak, çalgılar meyanına koymak şâyân-ı tecviz olmayan bir fiil bulunduğu zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Quran is actually recited in an unsuitable place such as a bathhouse, the reader sins, but the listener must still listen; failing to listen is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: hamamda Kur’an kıraat eden günaha girer, bununla beraber okunduğu takdirde dinlememek de sevab değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recording is at least a doubtful trace of recitation because it signifies inner speech; listening is permissible and preferable, disrespect is forbidden, and one should move Quran from an unworthy place.
rows.anchor: Zira bir kıraat değilse de bir şübhe-i kıraattir. Çünkü kelâm-ı nefsîye dâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God inwardly and verbally with supplication and fear; use a voice below public loudness but audible to oneself, in words of recitation, prayer, or other remembrance that do not obstruct thought.
rows.anchor: bir tazarru‘suretiyle ve bir nevi havf ile yalvararak ve korkarak kalben ve fikren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make inward remembrance a regular practice morning and evening, keeping the heart awake and constantly remembering God rather than among the heedless.
rows.anchor: Kalbin dâima uyanık ve zikrullahda dâim olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unusual bond between soul and body displays heart-consciousness and the unity of the self; through it a moment of awareness of God's oneness dawns.
rows.anchor: Nefs-i insânîde rûh ile bedenin pek acîb bir alâkası vardır ki vicdân-ı kalb ve vahdet-i nefsiye bu alâkada tecellî eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effects in the soul can descend into the body: imagining sourness makes the teeth ache, while imagining tragedy can cause headache, heat, or fainting.
rows.anchor: en âdî bir misâl olmak üzere bir ekşi tahayyülünden diş kamaşır ve bir fâcia tahayyülünden baş ağrısı, harâret veya baygınlık hâsıl olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reverse also occurs: repeating bodily acts forms a strong disposition in the soul.
rows.anchor: bu da bedenden rûha çıkan âsârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When spoken remembrance is audible to oneself without hindering thought, it creates an image in imagination; light rises to the soul and reflects through soul, tongue, imagination, and intellect, mutually strengthening them.
rows.anchor: bu zikr-i lisânîden hayâlde bir eser husûle gelir. Ve bundan rûha bir nûr yükselir, sonra bu envâr rûhtan lisâna, lisândan hayâle, hayâlden akla in‘ikas eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of this ascent have no limit; the journey of knowing seeks God through the endless sea, with the self as its ship and remembrance as its rudder.
rows.anchor: Sefer-i ma‘rifet işte bu nihâyetsiz deryâda matlûb-ı Hakk’a yürümektir. Bu seyrin yegâne gemisi nefis ve yegâne dümeni zikrullahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete heedlessness is a grave danger, and even a moment of heedlessness may be perilous.
rows.anchor: Gaflet-i külliye hatar-ı mutlak ve her gaflet lahzası bile bir hatar-ı muhtemildir

none: The segment contains only translated verse text and no commentary.
